subject: math
explanation: A power (or exponent) is a compact way to write repeated multiplication. In aⁿ, a is the base and n is the exponent — meaning a is multiplied by itself n times. Instead of writing 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 × 2, we write 2⁸. Powers are mathematical shorthand, like "kg" is shorter than "kilogram". Special cases: a¹ = a (exponent 1 changes nothing), and a⁰ = 1 for any non-zero a.

brainstorming.question: Why do we write powers at all?
brainstorming.answer: Because numbers can become enormous. 10¹⁰⁰ would require writing 10 one hundred times — powers save time and space.

brainstorming.question: Why is 2³ called "2 cubed"?
brainstorming.answer: 2³ = 8 can represent the volume of a cube with side 2. Similarly 2² represents area of a square — hence "squared".

brainstorming.question: Why is any number raised to power 0 equal to 1?
brainstorming.answer: Observe: 2⁴=16, 2³=8, 2²=4, 2¹=2. Each step divides by 2, so 2⁰=1. The pattern demands it.

misconceptions.correct: 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. Exponent means repeated multiplication, not multiplication by the exponent.
Exponent means repeated multiplication, not addition.

misconceptions.wrong: Any number raised to power 0 equals 0

realLifeConnections.title: Computer storage
realLifeConnections.description: Computers use powers of 2: 2¹⁰ = 1024 bytes, 2²⁰ ≈ 1 MB, 2³⁰ ≈ 1 GB.

realLifeConnections.title: Viral social media growth
realLifeConnections.description: One person shares with 2 friends, each shares with 2 more: Day 1→2, Day 2→4, Day 3→8 — powers in action.

realLifeConnections.title: Chessboard rice problem
realLifeConnections.description: Legend: 1 grain on first square, 2 on second, 4 on third — numbers explode rapidly through powers.

realLifeConnections.title: Compound interest
realLifeConnections.description: Money grows through repeated multiplication — banks and investors care about exponents.

activities.title: Paper folding activity
activities.instructions: Fold a paper 1, 2, 3, 4 times. Observe layers: 2, 4, 8, 16 — this demonstrates powers.

activities.title: Rice grain activity
activities.instructions: Draw 8 chessboard squares. Place 1, 2, 4, 8 grains on successive squares. Observe how quickly powers grow.

quiz.question: In 5³, the base is:
quiz.explanation: The base is the repeated number: 5.

quiz.question: What is 7⁰?
quiz.explanation: Any non-zero number to power 0 equals 1.

quiz.question: Why do mathematicians use powers?
quiz.explanation: Powers are shorthand for repeated multiplication.
